description: Base 5 (builds on Base 4, voice-b7260e73, folder Two Finger Gripper/versions/v304_generalist_one_piece_drive; related: Base 3): Look at the most recent design and see if you can come up with one that uses a single gear. Today the handles are driven through meshing gears, each handle sitting in a cradle on its own gear. Base 5 should open and close both fingers from the one RobStride RS00 using only one gear. Options: one central gear driving both handles through a rack, a cam or linkage, or an opposed rack-and-pinion where one pinion moves two opposing racks. Pick the simplest approach and briefly explain why you chose it over the others. Keep it parameterized, cut the part count below Base 4's 13 pieces where possible, keep the strap slots clear across the full travel, and record the count in VERSIONS.txt.

results.identified_issue: Jake rejected Base 5 (opposed-rack parallel gripper) on 2026-10-20 and chose Base 7 (Base 4 simplified for printability), which other pebbles track. Only docs changed: one line in VERSIONS.txt under the v305 entry and a banner at the top of v305 README. publish_designs.py reads only the VERSIONS.txt heading up to the first ':', so the extra line doesn't affect parsing. Base 5 is still in publish_designs.py generations and poses.js, so it still appears in the gallery. I left that alone because Jake said to keep the design.
results.summary: Got it: Base 5 is shelved. I left its folder as it is and marked it rejected so no agent builds on it. Base 7 takes over.
results.detailed_description: I didn't change any Base 5 design files. v305_generalist_single_gear stays exactly as it was. I added a 'Rejected 2026-10-20, do not build on Base 5, Base 7 replaces it' note in two places: under its VERSIONS.txt entry and at the top of its README. That way a future agent won't pick it up as the latest Base. It still shows in the live preview's Base picker. If you'd rather hide it there, say so.

results.notes: Wrong approach — going with Base 7 (Base 4 simplified for printability) instead. Keep the Base 5 design folder; do not build further on Base 5.

results.identified_issue: Mechanism choice: a pinion between opposed racks (parallel jaws) instead of keeping pivoting fingers. Pivoting with one gear needs a separate centreline rack plus pin-in-slot links (7 printed parts), and a centred crank or cam can't give mirror-symmetric motion. Consequences: open_d(a)=stroke*sin(a)/sin(max_angle) replaces the swing in placed(); poses.js has hinges:[] plus slides dir=±pose_dir (40), and test_gripper_poses.py checks the dir against the scad's pose_dir. gallery.js buildMix uses the base's pose when it has slides. check_gripper_closure.py skips designs with no hinges (it zips over an empty list). The pinion does not turn in the gallery: there is no motion type for it. Part count dropped 13 -> 12 only by moving the base from 3 to 2 front-ring M3 (at 30 and 210 deg, with both dowels); no load test backs that. Rack teeth are straight-sided 20 deg with no tip relief; the mesh is checked as solids only (Manifold intersections over 31 slider samples). A stroke above ~25 mm trips an assert (the top rack would reach the left arm). Not published here: Vigil/publisher rebuilds the catalog.
results.summary: Base 5: one pinion between two opposed racks drives both fingers. That's one gear instead of three, and 12 pieces instead of 13. The fingers now slide instead of swing.
results.detailed_description:
Base 5 is in Two Finger Gripper/versions/v305_generalist_single_gear. The pinion on the RS00 sits between two racks, one along its top (right finger) and one along its bottom (left finger). Turning it moves the two racks in opposite directions by exactly the same distance, so the fingers open and close symmetrically by construction.

Why this one: (1) Driving the swinging handles from one central rack needs an extra printed slider plus a pin-in-slot joint on each handle, and pushes the motor off-centre. (2) A cam only pushes one way, so it needs a return spring. A crank on one centred motor can't move two mirror-image handles by the same amount, so the fingers would meet off-centre. (3) Opposed racks give symmetry for free, and each rack merges into its handle just like Base 4's handle-gears did.

The trade-off you should weigh: the fingers now SLIDE (a parallel gripper) instead of swinging. Closed, they sit exactly where Base 4's did, so the tip contact is unchanged. Fully open, the tips are only 40 mm apart (stroke 20 mm per side; the Tune slider goes to 25). Base 4's 30-degree swing opened them about 125 mm.

What changed:
- Each handle-rack keeps Base 4's plate, strap tunnel, tail, hub and floor, so the finger still drops in from above.
- A tongue under each rack runs in a groove in the base, and the groove ends act as travel stops. Base 3 and 4 had none.
- The side gears, axles and bushings are gone.
- The base now uses 2 of the motor's front-ring screws instead of 3; the two dowels still locate it.

Count: 6 printed parts (2 fingers, 2 handle-racks, pinion, base) + RS00 + 5 M3 = 12. Base 4 was 13. This is recorded in VERSIONS.txt.

All 34 geometry checks pass. The strap tunnel mouths stay clear over the full travel. The pinion meshes both racks from 0 to 30 on the slider and jams half a tooth off. Each rack hits its stop 0.5 mm past open or closed.

New Tune params: stroke, gear_module, rack_back, rack_clear, rack_margin, arm_w, key_w, key_h, base_margin.

Gallery: poses.js moves Base 5 with slides, not hinges. Mix-and-match follows those slides whenever Base 5 is picked. test_gripper_poses.py now covers slide designs.

Not verified: nothing printed. Peak motor torque puts about 640 N on the module-2 teeth, which is a lot for PLA, so cap the motor torque. Nothing holds the racks down in the grooves except gravity.

summary: Base 5 tried driving both gripper fingers from one RS00 with a single pinion between two opposed racks, but it was rejected. Base 7, a printability-simplified Base 4, replaces it, and the Base 5 folder stays untouched.
